findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error
findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable audit file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> (or a domain error enum) and propagate the I/O error with ? or explicit map_err

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid digit input or out-of-range values
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV value aborts the entire audit load instead of returning a typed parse error for the offending record
findings.fix: Use map_err or ? to propagate ParseIntError, and return a Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> (or domain error enum)

findings.problem: Lossy as cast: .unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value in [65536..max] silently wraps to an incorrect u16, corrupting audit data with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) and return an error when the value exceeds u16::MAX, or parse directly to u16 if the domain guarantees it

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[0] without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with zero fields causes a panic via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use get(0).ok_or(...) or split_once(',') to safely extract the first field

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[1] without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A line with only one comma-separated field causes a panic via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') for first-separator extraction per SKILL.md line 11, then parse the second part safely with get/map_err

findings.problem: println!() inside load_audits — hidden I/O side effect in data-parsing function
findings.failure_mode: The core/parsing layer has observable side effects, preventing deterministic testing and introducing logging coupling
findings.fix: Remove println!; if logging is needed, pass a logger sink or return a record that carries metadata, keeping the core pure

findings.problem: load_audits mixes file I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing and validation in a single function returning Vec
findings.failure_mode: Cannot test parsing logic in isolation; I/O errors, parse errors, and validation errors are all lost into a Vec or panic
findings.fix: Split into a shell function that reads bytes and delegates to a pure core function parse_records(&[u8]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError>

findings.problem: Collects all split parts into Vec<String> — cargo-cult heap allocation for a known 2-field record
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line increases memory pressure and GC pressure; prevents zero-copy parsing
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to get two &str fragments, trim each, and parse directly without collecting into Vec<String>

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_audits throughput or latency claims
findings.failure_mode: Unmeasured performance — the function allocates Vec<String> per line and clones String per record, but no evidence proves this is acceptable or optimal
findings.fix: Add a criterion or divan benchmark measuring lines-per-second and peak memory across representative file sizes

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_audits throughput or latency
no profiler data (perf, flamegraph) for allocation hot spots in the parsing loop
no allocation profiling (e.g., heaptrack, valgrind --massif) evidence for Vec<String> per-line overhead
no second-ring evidence (cargo-flamegraph, alloc-sampler, or similar) validating that the functional core is measurable as pure
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has 5 BLOCKER violations (unwrap on I/O, unwrap on parse, lossy as cast, 2x unchecked indexing, println! side effect) and 3 WARNING/INFO items (mixed I/O+parsing, cargo-cult Vec allocation, missing benchmarks). Fixing the BLOCKERs requires converting load_audits to return Result, using split_once + get for parsing, replacing as with try_from, and removing println!
